blockers.statement: The identifier leak that held this terminal is closed and the primary survives it. Episode identifiers crossing the provider boundary are now opaque handles, verified role-free against a 1000-permutation null on a role-stratified held-out split; the unchanged leakage audit passes on all 96 episode-arms where it previously failed on all 96, and every scored statistic is bit-identical to the identified run (ROLE_FREE_RERUN_V4, terminal P1_R6_NATIVE_PRIMARY_PASS_PENDING_2019_REPLICATION). Three things still stand between that and this terminal. The host is a frozen deterministic provider, which cannot exploit a leaked label, so identical scores there are close to true by construction rather than evidence about a semantic model. Evaluator custody is internal -- the evaluator is authored in the same lane as the candidate -- and PROTECTED_SUPERIORITY admits only PROSPECTIVE_PROTECTED evidence, which requires external custody. And the terminal the run reports is itself conditional on the 2019 replication that P1-U-T2 is blocked on.
blockers.unblock: Three steps, in this order, none of which is the identifier work -- that is done. Re-run the now-clean boundary against a changed semantic host, where the identical-scores finding becomes a real result instead of a property of a provider that cannot read. Move evaluator custody outside the authoring lane, since no amount of internal re-running reaches PROSPECTIVE_PROTECTED. And unblock P1-U-T2 by removing the hardcoded source_year == 2020, because the terminal this run reports is pending that replication by its own name. One residual is recorded and deliberately not repaired: the words 'adverse' and 'control' occur in dossier text at in-sample informedness 0.000 and 0.072 over 5 of 88 payloads, which is incidental scientific vocabulary rather than an encoded label, and repairing corpus content during an identifier repair would change the arena mid-run.

blockers.statement: The blocker this replaces named PR #733 as in-flight upstream work. #733 was closed unmerged on 2026-08-21, superseded by #752, which also closed unmerged after running. So nothing is in flight, and two completed campaigns now exist whose results the ledger had not recorded. V2 never scored: its repeated-pid crosswalk probe returned HTTP 200 with an empty results array, below its prospectively frozen minimum of one, so acquisition never started. V3 changed the crosswalk encoding, did run all 400 rows, and terminated P2_WIDE_EXTERNAL_V3_CANNOT_CHECK on provider validity: 0.716 against a frozen 0.90. Underneath that correct terminal is a harder finding, measured rather than asserted (P2_COMPARISON_RESOLUTION_2026-08-22). Both completed campaigns ran at the measurement floor. The frozen rule requires an average-IoU delta of 0.03 before superiority is supported, and every arm in both campaigns scores about 0.004, so the entire measured performance of the best arm is smaller than the difference the campaign exists to detect. Deleting a competing arm outright would not reach the threshold. Everything else follows: all 399 paired questions tie, the bootstrap interval is [0.0, 0.0] which reads as the strongest possible equivalence evidence and is instead the signature of an instrument with no resolution, and in V3 three distinct candidate files produced one byte-identical evaluator output. In V1 the three arms shared one candidate digest outright, so that campaign scored a single system against itself three times.
blockers.unblock: Raise the arms off the floor before running another campaign; a fourth transport version scored at IoU 0.004 would spend the same effort to learn the same nothing. That means finding out why retrieval scores near zero on a benchmark whose own gold is reachable -- which the resolution audit deliberately does not diagnose, because it measures the instrument and not the retrieval. Only then are the route families #650 enumerates worth building: missing-route, retrieved-but-unprocessed, duplicated, contradictory, provider-invalid, apparently-saturated. Independently of all of it, this terminal is PROTECTED_SUPERIORITY and admits only PROSPECTIVE_PROTECTED evidence, which requires external evaluator custody that no campaign here has had.

blockers.statement: This is the terminal the resolution finding matters most to, because a non-inferiority guard is exactly what a degenerate interval would wrongly discharge. Both completed Wide campaigns report a paired interval of [0.0, 0.0] over 399 matched questions with 399 ties, no wins and no losses. Read at face value that is conclusive equivalence. It is instead a zero-width interval over identical differences, which a bootstrap produces at any sample size, and it arises because every arm sits at the measurement floor -- about 0.004 average IoU against a frozen required delta of 0.03. Route-level and task-level closure receipts over a naturalistic arena are still missing, which was the original statement and remains true; what is added is that the instrument that would carry them currently has no resolution, so collecting receipts through it would produce another interval that could not have come out any other way. Three reporting defects travel with both artifacts: they publish the unseeded max_iou_at_k family that the paper's own score_wide_comparison.py excludes by rule, that family decreases in k which a maximum over the top k cannot do, and every runtime total is exactly zero, which is untransported measurement rather than measured cost.
blockers.unblock: Require the resolution audit to pass before a campaign's paired interval is allowed to discharge anything: an interval from an all-ties split, from arms whose evaluator output is byte-identical, or from arms below the campaign's own frozen effect threshold must map to CANNOT_CHECK rather than to non-inferiority. Then require closure receipts per route and per task in the campaign schema before outcomes are accessed. The guard exists and reports both campaigns as ZERO_RESOLUTION; wiring it into the campaign's own terminal rule is the step that has not been taken.

blockers.statement: There is no identifiability audit, and without one no score from this benchmark can be used at all -- that is what H3 taught. A partial one now exists and finds the lesson was learned too narrowly. H3's saturation was diagnosed as label recoverability and repaired on that axis, but saturation is checkable directly from any published panel: read each metric across every system and ask whether it takes more than one value. Done that way (P4_PANEL_RESOLUTION_2026-08-22), the published V2 panel decides two of its three hypotheses on metrics no system varies on. clean_coverage is exactly 1.0 for all eleven systems, so H2 -- the clean-coverage non-inferiority guard -- reports [0.0, 0.0] and PASS, which is a guard no system in the panel can fail. correct_cannot_check_rate is also 1.0 for all eleven, so H3 reports [0.0, 0.0] and NOT_SUPPORTED, a negative that records the benchmark rather than the systems. Saturation is not a bias toward optimism: in the same panel it produced one PASS and one NOT_SUPPORTED. The later identifiable V3 panel repairs correct_cannot_check_rate, which varies there, and leaves clean_coverage saturated at 1.0 across every system. Only false_promotion_rate discriminates in either panel, ranging 0.0 to 0.917, and H1's interval is earned.
blockers.unblock: Make the identifiability audit a precondition gate that runs before any score is read, not a post-hoc report -- and give it the saturation check as its cheapest leg, since that one needs only the panel and would have refused H2 in both constructions. Then the harder leg the H3 lesson actually names: labels provably unrecoverable from evidence-list length, missingness pattern, template or source count. A clean-coverage guard also needs a construction on which some system fails it; until one exists, non-inferiority on that metric cannot be claimed from a panel where every system is perfect.

Carries a control panel whose every metric discriminates, and each check is tested against a case it must not fire on -- an interior saturation, a floor/ceiling split, a missing rate that must not be read as zero, and a one-case rate difference that must not be absorbed as float noise. Real work and it discharges nothing: it takes no view on whether a saturated metric is the wrong metric, which needs a system that fails and these panels do not contain one.

evidence.notes: Eleven theorems discharged by Z3 over uninterpreted sorts, so neither is a finite instance. Separation: separated commutation, the converse that separation is necessary, write locality, frame determinacy and fixpoint conservativity, with the state transformer left an uninterpreted function under a frame condition -- commutation is therefore a property of separation and not of the modular arithmetic P6's finite check instantiated. Reopening: soundness, completeness, minimality, conservativity, monotonicity and the cycle characterisation over dependency graphs of any size, cyclic or not, over an uninterpreted node sort. Both specifications are written independently of P6's implementations, and both implementations are then shown to be instances rather than assumed to be: apply_local_mechanic obeys its declared frame on all 5,280 exhaustive perturbations, and descendants agrees with the independent specification on 61,440 of 61,440 directed graphs over four nodes and changed subsets, 51,712 of them with a non-empty reopening. Two limits travel with the mechanization and are stated in the artifacts: reachability is axiomatised as a reflexive-transitive closure carrying a well-founded rank, because transitive closure is not first-order definable, and an earlier axiomatisation without the rank admitted circular reachability -- a differential against the committed implementation caught it. Independent review of these proofs is P6-U-T4 and is not claimed here.

The finite result now follows from the theorem discharged at P6-U-T1 rather than from a second theory standing beside it. P6's certificate model is interpreted into the reopening signature -- a certificate over n coordinates is the star graph on n+1 nodes, damage is a changed set on the coordinate nodes, repair removes coordinates from it -- and six theorems are discharged by Z3 over an uninterpreted node sort at any width: any damage withdraws the certificate, a full repair restores it, a partial repair does not, undamaged coordinates are never collateral damage, the dependency runs one way, and the certificate supports nothing. The published 155 full restorations and 1,055 proper-subset failures are then recomputed by running the committed descendants over the interpreted graph -- the same implementation P6-U-T1 verified against the independent specification on 61,440 of 61,440 cases -- so the counts are output of a verified instance of the theorems rather than a separate enumeration that happens to agree. The interpretation is shown to be carrying the proof rather than the counts: each of its three frame conditions loses at least one theorem when dropped. A fourth frame condition was removed because the same check reported it inert; it and one other were a redundant presentation of the same constraint, and it is now discharged as a theorem instead of assumed. The counts on their own do not identify the interpretation, and that is measured rather than glossed: a chain running through the coordinates into the certificate, the star with coordinate cross-edges and the complete graph each reproduce 1,055 exactly, because the pair tests whether every coordinate reaches the certificate and nothing further -- leaving that reachability class moves it to 975 or collapses it to 0. All three indistinguishable graphs are refuted by a theorem instead: each reopens coordinates as collateral damage, which UNDAMAGED_COORDINATES_ARE_NOT_REOPENED forbids and which the shipped implementation is confirmed not to do on the star. So the proof pins the graph and the counts confirm its reachability class. Separately, the 1,536-state lift rule is derived from three primitives about certificates and embeddings, reproducing scientific_admissible everywhere with both verdicts present, and P6's own revalidation assertion block accepts the derived rule while rejecting three weakenings of it. Two limits are on the record rather than implied: 155 is not discriminating -- every wrong graph and every weakened primitive returns it, because a full repair leaves nothing changed -- and the five donor families enter neither the graph nor the changed set, so 155 and 1,055 are 31 and 211 counted five times. Independent review is P6-U-T4 and is not claimed here.

evidence.notes: A general compositional calculus, discharged by Z3 over uninterpreted sorts, so identity, associativity and intermediate-contract composition hold for any number of transformations, contracts, coordinates and obligations and for every donor-native predicate rather than for the five families P7 enumerates. The side conditions are stated rather than assumed away: identity needs the contract test to be reflexive, the strict equational laws need extensionality, and obligation-totality composition needs containment of demanded obligations rather than a registered bridge. One result of the mechanization is negative and is kept: P7's composition rule is provably incomplete against its own obligation semantics, refusing composites whose contracts demand exactly the same obligations when no bridge is registered. This terminal asks whether the general calculus exists, and it does; whether P7's finite results are instances of it is P7-U-T2 and is separately blocked, and independent reproduction is P7-U-T5.

P7's finite composition result now follows from the calculus discharged at P7-U-T1 rather than standing beside it. The five donor families are interpreted as a transformation family: each is a transformation with its own source and target obligation contracts, and the bridge_match the committed runner types as a literal becomes Match(Tgt t, Src u), computed from the two transformations and the registered bridge relation -- which is the open item research/failures/2026-08-supplied-premise-unbuilt-decision left for the theory lane, done here for the finite result. Under three frame conditions -- hand-offs are never contract identities, distinct families have distinct endpoints, the stack is inhabited -- twelve theorems are discharged by Z3 over uninterpreted transformation, contract, coordinate and obligation sorts for a donor stack of any size: a bridged hand-off composes, an unbridged one refuses, a donor composed with itself still needs a bridge, either leg failing refuses, the hand-off identifies the donor pair, distinct hand-offs can differ in verdict, both halves are non-vacuous on an inhabited stack, and a three-donor chain needs every interior bridge. Two further conditions were written as axioms first, came back inert from the load-bearing check, and are discharged as theorems instead. The published 25 successes and 25 bridge countermodels are recomputed by running the committed carries and compose with the hand-off computed rather than supplied, and the six argument triples the shipped loop never reaches are exercised on those same functions over 204,800 evaluations spanning all eight triples with both verdicts present. Three negatives are on the record rather than smoothed. The published counts still reach only 2 of compose's 8 argument triples, because reproducing 25 and 25 requires two uniform registries over an all-carrying stack -- the 25 rows are now 25 distinct hand-offs rather than 25 copies of one argument, but they are still 25 agreeing verdicts, and P7 shipped no registry that would separate them. The 25 successes discriminate nothing about the interpretation: every contract assignment tried returns 25 under a registry that bridges everything. And the counts cannot see the second frame condition at all -- two readings in which the 5x5 loop visits one and five distinct hand-offs reproduce both published numbers exactly -- so what establishes that the donor axis indexes anything is THE_HANDOFF_IDENTIFIES_THE_DONOR_PAIR and the measured hand-off count, not the published pair. Independent formal or empirical reproduction is P7-U-T5 and is not claimed here.

evidence.notes: Ten composition and revocation theorems for P8's formal core, discharged by Z3 over uninterpreted domain, object and issuer sorts, so they are not statements about the thirteen donor families P8 enumerates. Two limits travel with the mechanization and are in the artifact: reachability is axiomatised as a reflexive-transitive closure carrying a well-founded rank, because transitive closure is not first-order definable, and the chain theorem's induction schema is the single hand step. The rank is not a formality -- an earlier axiomatisation without it admitted circular reachability, in which a sink domain reached its own source, and a differential against the committed implementation is what caught it. This terminal asks whether the general theorem is proved and mechanized, and it is; whether P8's exhaustive finite result is an instance of it is P8-U-T2, which the 3,072-state donor interpretation answers for the state model but not for the 169 heterogeneous chain compositions, and independent reproduction is P8-U-T5.

And the donor axis is inert -- 239,616 sibling pairs differing only in donor family, zero verdict-changing.

The interpretation step P8-U-T1's unblock named. Each of the seven arguments X4's terminal takes is assigned to the calculus conjunct it means -- type-coordinate agreement or a registered coercion is the calculus's Reach, narrowing is scope containment, the blocker is simultaneously an obligation and a defeater -- and the calculus rule under that assignment reproduces X4 exactly on all 3,072 distinct states, with all four terminals reached (BLOCK 1181, CANNOT_CHECK 256, DISCHARGE 99, NO_DONOR_AUTHORITY 1536). A derivation rather than a transcription: three independent changes to X4's semantics each break soundness.

blockers.unblock: Execute cells. The ladder needs real model scales, which this environment cannot provide -- and the freeze explicitly refuses a surrogate, because a classical-learner capacity ladder is not a model-scale ladder and substituting one would answer a different question. Any cell left unexecuted keeps the whole grid at CANNOT_CHECK by construction; a fully executed grid with no evaluable crossing test is also CANNOT_CHECK, not a pass.

blockers.statement: The representation-length and format-prior attacks have now been run, and one of them succeeds. Length does not explain the typed arm; it explains most of the untyped comparator, which drops 0.906 to 0.609 under an equal-token control while typed holds 1.0. Format prior does succeed: TYPED_SERIALIZED_BAG moves 0.75 to 0.50 under a bijection on the value alphabet that preserves every gold label, so the published typed-minus-serialized margin measures which symbols were drawn rather than the information the representation carries. The surviving margin is the one the existing failure record already identified, TYPED_RELATIONAL minus UNTYPED_PAIR at +0.09375, whose both arms are orbit-invariant.
